messages:
miguel: Heads up - paging shows suppressed for a bunch of alerts from pageflow around 03:26 UTC. Looks like the proxy truncated the paging header. Customers might have missed pages. :fire:
ops-bot: Alert posted to #incidents: pageflow.proxy.header_truncate (severity: high)
kevin: Oncall here, paging? did phone pages go out or just slack messages?
sara: quick check - slack notifications reached the channel but pager gateway got 400s. extracted snippets from gateway logs:
```
time=2026-03-11T03:25:58Z svc=pager-gateway status=400 err="header too long" header_len=16384 truncated=true
```
kevin: ugh. that explains it. paging provider dropped on 400. Are we sure proxy changed limits? @sara can you confirm recent deploys? :eyes:
sara: I rolled a config bump to pageflow-proxy yesterday to tighten header sanitation (trying to stop X-Trace spam). I didn't expect it to chop Authorization-* + paging-metadata. quick mitigation: add a passthrough rule for headers starting with "X-Pager-" and increase max_header_size to 48KB on the proxy. patch below (hotfix):
```
proxy.headers.allow_prefix: ["X-Pager-"]
proxy.headers.max_size: 49152
```
miguel: Customer impact: Support ticket #CS-1129 reports missed operator pages between 03:24-03:44 (one customer on Dedicated plan). Severity unclear but they missed a critical oncall page.
kevin: I'll kick off manual paging and follow runbook for missed-pager escalation. tagging ops for phone call.
sara: I'm going to push the proxy hotpatch to canary now, will monitor kv metrics and gateway 4xx.
deploy-bot: hotpatch canary deploy started for pageflow-proxy (deploy/patch-2026-03-11-01).
ops-bot: Manual page triggered for CS-1129, triage in progress.
miguel: Thanks. Once canary looks good, let's roll to prod and create an incident ticket with timeline + customers affected. I'll draft initial incident body. :memo:
